title: An exact split assigned 45% of the thermal shift at 21 Finnish moth sites to recorded occurrence
abstract: An earlier analysis assigned 77% of a Finnish moth thermal shift to species recorded in both endpoint windows. We split that resident term into annual recorded occurrence and positive catch share. At 21 sites with at least five surveys in 1993-2002 and 2013-2022, the 0.248 C shift contained 0.054 C from resident occurrence, 0.136 C from positive catch share, 0.052 C from entry and 0.005 C from loss. Occurrence-related terms thus supplied 45%, with a spatial-block interval of 31-68%. Positive catch share supplied 71% of resident change, but its crossed year-and-block interval was 40-93%, which includes equal shares. Pooled raw counts gave a similar split. A pooled-presence negative control gave zero positive-count contribution. The exact four-part method makes separate constraints for occurrence and positive catches. It does not identify demographic rates, climate causation or a cause of weak tracking in other networks. Source overlap, detection, selected southern sites and limited temporal uncertainty restrict inference. Code, aggregate estimates, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: The exact four-part split and sensitivity checks. Spatial-block intervals condition on years; the crossed check also resamples common calendar years.
